name: Electrician Apprenticeship (Forsyth County Electrical Contractors Association, at Forsyth Tech)
sourceWorkbook: Forsyth Tech: the catalog's Programs Offered tables 2021–22 through 2026–27 (D35130, C35130, CIP 46.0302, day; the diploma marked REVISED for 2026–27), the 2025–26 Electrical Systems Technology diploma and certificate pages (term lines and the 39- and 15-credit totals), the program pages (one-year diploma, 1–2-semester certificate, 2100 Silas Creek Pkwy), the 2023 Career & College Promise booklet (C35130P1), the Technical Career Path page, the Careers Electric coverage (WFDD 2026-07-13, NCBCE and EdNC 2026-06), the FCECA apprenticeship page and its published sections, the Workforce Continuing Education catalog page (144 classroom hours a year, 2,000 OJT hours, the NCDOL Journeyman's card), the Installation/Troubleshooting course page, the 2026–27 academic calendar and the course schedule's summer 2026 electrical sections; course hours and credits from the NCCCS Combined Course Library; sequences as the 2025–26 tables give them — compiled 2026-11-18
note: The four-year Forsyth County Electrical Contractors Association apprenticeship taught at Forsyth Tech (Workforce Continuing Education; SOC 47-2111): each level is one year, fall through spring, with at least 144 hours of classroom instruction a year and 2,000 hours of on-the-job training a year (the catalog); graduates receive a Journeyman's Card from the NC Department of Labor. Carried on the college's published sections: a fall term of 16 weeks at two 2.5-hour evenings (80 hours, the published 8.00 CEU) and a spring term of 35 evenings (87.5 hours, 8.75 CEU) — 167.5 hours a level, 670 in all — Level 1 Tue/Thu 7:00–9:30 PM in Robert L. Strickland Center 1250, Level 2 Mon/Wed 6:30–9:00 PM at the Strickland Center (a second section Tue/Thu at West Campus), Level 4 Tue/Thu 6:00–8:30 PM at the Strickland Center; no Level 3 section was found, so its evenings carry no day or time. $240 a semester; apprentices must be 18, register in the fall, and complete the fall class before the spring class; those not employed by an electrical contractor may enroll and pay the fees. On-the-job hours are recorded on each level, not scheduled. Which contractors employ the apprentices, the class size and the apprenticeship's ApprenticeshipNC registration number are not published. Contact: James Mitchell, 336.734.7771. Class size 16 is a stand-in.
weeklyHoursNote: Term hours per student are the catalog's weekly contact hours × 16 (the 16-week basis), whatever the term's length: the sessions carry them, the posted days, times and rooms place them. Hours and credits are the NCCCS course standard's; every credit course carries its hours with no section on record at the Main Campus (the lab building is not published); the apprenticeship sits on its published evenings at the Strickland Center and the Installation/Troubleshooting course on its published Mon/Wed evenings at West Campus; clinical hours are zero in every course.
